title: multi-sdks: unify auth/retries + streaming ergonomics + parity bumps (v1.200.1)
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: customer and internal SDK parity gaps around auth token refresh + retry semantics and streaming ergonomics cause inconsistent developer experience across Python/TS/Go. This PR unifies the auth retry strategy, standardizes streaming event shapes and APIs, and bumps SDK package versions to v1.200.1 for parity. Summary of changes: 1) Introduce shared auth client contract and server-backed token refresh helper; add exponential backoff + jitter canonical implementation used by all SDKs; ensure retriable http/gRPC errors are normalized. 2) Streaming API ergonomics: make event shapes consistent (data/error/done/heartbeat), add typed helpers for TypeScript and Go to consume chunked responses, and expose a small high-level iterate_stream convenience API in Python. 3) Parity fixes and minor API renames to align naming across SDKs (AuthClient -> TokenProvider, StreamEvent -> StreamMessage). 4) Changelog, docs updates, and package version bumps (python: v1.200.1, typescript: v1.200.1, go: v1.200.1). Includes updated examples and migration notes. Testing: unit tests added for retry/backoff, integration smoke tests for streaming across all runtimes, and e2e auth refresh scenario simulated in CI. Backwards compatibility: default retry/backoff values are conservative and opt-outs are provided via explicit config; migration guide included in docs.

release_notes: Unify auth token refresh and retry semantics across SDKs; standardize streaming API shapes and add ergonomic helpers; bump SDK packages to v1.200.1 with migration notes. No breaking changes by default; opt-out/config provided.
migration_guide: See docs/sdk/migration-v1.200.1.md for migration steps: rename AuthClient->TokenProvider (optional), update to new RetryConfig, and use iterate_stream / stream helpers for consistent streaming consumption.
notes: This PR was coordinated with the platform team to ensure server-side compatibility for token refresh endpoints. The shared package is intentionally small to keep SDK surface minimal. Post-merge actions: publish all three SDK packages, monitor telemetry for retry saturation, and run rollback plan if auth regressions appear.
example_usage: Python: with client.iterate_stream(prompt) as it: for msg in it: handle(msg) | TypeScript: for await (const msg of client.stream(prompt)) { handle(msg) } | Go: decoder := client.Stream(ctx, req); for decoder.Next() { msg := decoder.Message(); handle(msg) }
